Summary — Archery at the 2012 Summer Olympics, Women's team

Quick facts
- Dates: 27–29 July 2012
- Venue: Lord’s Cricket Ground, London
- Competitors: 36 (12 teams, 3 archers per team)
- Medalists: Gold — South Korea (KOR); Silver — China (CHN); Bronze — Japan (JPN)

Event format (how the competition worked)
- Each country fielded a team of three female recurve archers.
- All archers shot a 72‑arrow individual ranking round (at 70 m). The three individual scores for each country were summed to produce that team’s ranking‑round total and seed.
- Twelve teams qualified to the team competition and were seeded 1–12 by ranking‑round total. The Olympic team elimination bracket gave byes to the top four seeded teams into the quarterfinals; seeds 5–12 contested the first elimination round to reach the quarters.
- Team matches were contested under the cumulative scoring format used at the time: each team shot a fixed number of arrows per match and the higher total score advanced. (If you want the exact number of arrows per match and the end structure used in 2012, I can give that detail.)

Notable points and context
- South Korea continued its long dominance in Olympic women’s team archery by winning the gold medal in London. The Korean women have been the strongest nation in women's Olympic team archery for decades.
- The competition took place on the outfield at Lord’s Cricket Ground, an iconic and unusual setting for archery at the Olympics which attracted attention for its atmosphere and spectator experience.
